title: Driving Eligibility and Legal Vehicle Use

location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Anyone driving in Bali must comply with Indonesian driving-licence requirements and use a legally operated vehicle appropriate for the journey.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Governor Circular requires foreign tourists operating vehicles to hold a valid national or international driving licence and use four-wheeled transport from legally registered rental businesses or associations. Kejati Bali's FAQ summarizes licence and vehicle-document expectations.
content.significance: A valid licence and legally operated vehicle help ensure drivers are authorized and vehicles can be identified by authorities.
common_situations: Being stopped at a traffic checkpoint

do: Confirm your licence is valid for the vehicle class and recognized in Indonesia
Carry required driving and vehicle documents
Use a properly registered rental provider and check roadworthiness
dont: Drive without the required valid licence
Assume a home-country licence alone is sufficient
Use a rental vehicle when its legal status is unclear

common_misconceptions: Renting a scooter does not itself authorize someone to ride it.
regional_variations: Underlying driving rules are national; the Bali circular reiterates obligations for foreign tourists.
content.additional_notes: For legal questions, refer users to Indonesian Police or the relevant licensing authority. Do not make individualized legal determinations.

sources.title: Bali Governor Circular Letter No. 07 of 2025 on Foreign Tourist Conduct
Foreigner Legal Service — Traffic Law FAQ

verification.verification_notes: Core requirements are explicit in the 2025 circular; detailed document procedures should be checked against current authorities.

sensitivity.handling_notes: Use neutral, precise wording; distinguish formal rules from courtesy recommendations.
